h1: Designing a wine label that stands out on Indian store shelves
title: Wine Label Design for Indian Shelves | Craft Beer School
desc: How to design a wine label that gets noticed in Indian liquor stores: counter-service shelves, grape names, heat, ice buckets and rules.
teaser: Most Indian wine is bought from across a counter. Your label has about two seconds and two metres to work.
standfirst: A wine label in India has to work in conditions European design books never mention: counter-service stores, buyers who order by grape, humid storerooms and ice buckets. This guide covers what makes a label sell here.
sections: Know where the bottle is actually sold

In many Indian states most liquor is bought at a counter. The buyer stands behind a grille and points at a shelf two or three metres away. Small type, subtle embossing and pale colours vanish at that distance.

Premium walk-in stores, airport duty free and restaurant lists are different. There the label is seen up close and can carry finer detail. Before you brief a designer, find out which channel sells most of your volume. A label designed for a boutique store in Mumbai can disappear on a busy counter in a smaller town.
What the buyer looks for first

Indian wine buyers, especially newer ones, tend to scan for three things: the type of wine, the grape and the price. Brand comes later.

  • Make the style obvious. Red, white, rosé or sparkling should be clear from the bottle and label colour together.
  • Name the grape clearly. Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon are the names many buyers recognise. Put the grape where it can be read at shelf distance.
  • Use a single strong brand mark. A clear name or symbol that a buyer can ask for by name next time.

Our guide to reading a wine label shows the label from the buyer's side. It is worth reading before you design one.
What has to be on the label

Indian wine labels carry mandatory information under food safety and state excise rules. At a process level this typically includes the brand name, alcohol strength, volume, manufacturer details, FSSAI logo and licence number, batch or lot details and a statutory warning. Many states also require state-specific markings, permitted sale declarations or excise labels and holograms applied after printing.

The exact list, wording, type sizes and approval process vary by state and change over time. Label registration with the excise department is usually needed before a product can be sold. Check the current notification for every state you plan to sell in, or work with a licensing consultant. Our guide to beer label rules in India covers the same process for beer.

Leave space for these elements in the first sketch. Designers who add them at the end usually end up shrinking the brand to fit.
Design for heat, humidity and ice

Wine in India meets water. Bottles sweat when they come out of a cold store into a humid shop. Restaurants plunge whites into ice buckets. A plain paper label wrinkles, peels and turns grey within an hour.

  • Specify wet-strength paper or a film label for whites, rosé and sparkling wines.
  • Ask the printer for adhesive rated for chilled and wet conditions.
  • Test finished bottles in an ice bucket for an hour before approving the print run.
  • Avoid dark, flood-coated designs that show every scuff from transport.

This is the detail most new wine brands miss: a label that looked beautiful in the studio and slid off the bottle at the first restaurant.

The front label sells. Keep it simple: brand, grape, style and one visual idea. The back label informs. It carries the mandatory information, a short description of taste and a food suggestion that fits Indian meals. A line such as "crisp and fresh, good with tandoori fish and coastal curries" helps a buyer more than a paragraph about the vineyard.

A neck label or capsule colour can signal the range. Many wineries use colour to separate an entry range from a reserve range, so staff can find bottles quickly. Our guide to beer label design covers range architecture in more depth.

1. Print full-size mock-ups and stick them on real bottles.
  2. Put them on a real shelf, with competitors either side. Look at them from three metres.
  3. Ask people who buy wine occasionally, not your design team, what the wine is and what it might cost.
  4. Check the mandatory information against current rules for each state.
  5. Run the ice bucket test.

The design is only half the work. Turning a label into a brand that buyers remember is a separate skill, built from positioning, range planning and packaging choices working together.
faqs: Do wine labels need approval in India?

Generally yes. Labels are usually registered with the state excise department before sale, alongside food safety requirements. Rules vary by state, so check the current notification or ask a licensing consultant.
Should the grape name be large on the front label?
For most Indian buyers, yes. Many people choose by grape, so a clearly readable variety name helps the bottle sell.
What label material works for wine served in ice buckets?
Wet-strength paper or a film label with adhesive rated for wet, chilled use. Test real bottles in an ice bucket before approving a print run.
